findings.issue: AC-21 is a tautological happy-path test, not a failure-injection test. The test name 'test_ac21_attest_parity_rollback_on_db_failure' implies it tests the failure case, but no failure is injected — it simply calls attest_parity on the success path and asserts file==DB afterwards. It does NOT monkeypatch db.execute to raise after os.replace, so the divergence window (file renamed, DB update pending) is never exercised. This means R2 atomicity is NOT tested.
findings.fix: Monkeypatch db.execute (specifically the UPDATE campaigns SET claim_sha256 call) to raise after os.replace has already executed. Then assert: (a) the exception propagates, (b) the file SHA matches whatever state it was in before the attempted mutation OR a reconcile check catches it. The correct test requires real failure injection after the rename.

findings.issue: SHA encoding bug in test_ac21: file_sha is computed as hashlib.sha256(file_content.encode()).hexdigest() where file_content is str (text). But attest_parity computes new_sha256 via hashlib.sha256(new_content).hexdigest() where new_content = abs_claim_path.read_bytes() (bytes). For files containing only ASCII this is equivalent, but the semantic mismatch means the test would silently give a wrong result on any non-ASCII content. More critically: this means the test is not testing what attest_parity actually does — it is recomputing a SHA via a different code path, which could mask divergence.
findings.fix: Use Path.read_bytes() consistently: file_sha = hashlib.sha256((tmp_path / 'test_parity.claim.toml').read_bytes()).hexdigest(). Match the implementation exactly.

findings.issue: R2 divergence window is real and not self-healing. Sequence: (1) temp file written + fsynced; (2) os.replace(temp, claim_path) — atomic, POSIX-guaranteed; (3) new_content = read_bytes(); (4) new_sha256 = sha256(new_content); (5) db.execute UPDATE claim_sha256. A crash or exception between steps 2 and 5 leaves file=new/DB=old — diverged. check_sha() (line 445) raises ValueError on this mismatch, and conclude_campaign calls it before every Union Gate, so the campaign is permanently bricked. The exception handler at line 668 only cleans up if the rename FAILED (temp_path.exists()), but after a successful rename temp_path no longer exists — so the handler does nothing useful for the post-rename failure case. T5's design doc claim ('next check_sha() will catch it') is incorrect: catching means raising, which bricks.
findings.fix: Option A (safest for v1): make attest_parity idempotent/self-healing — on check_sha mismatch, recompute SHA from current file and update DB (a repair path). Option B: reverse ordering — DB update first, then rename. On crash: DB=new/file=old; check_sha raises but rerunning attest_parity is safe (idempotent). Option C: make check_sha self-heal: if file exists and SHA differs, recompute from file and update DB atomically. Any of these eliminates the brick-the-campaign failure mode.
